ambiguities: The passage attributes to Swann the belief that Odette was desired by every man at the hotel and desired them in turn ('il croyait qu'elle était désirée par tous les hommes... et qu'elle-même les désirait'); this is framed explicitly as Swann's jealous suspicion ('il croyait'), not a narrator-endorsed judgment of Odette's conduct, so it was not scored as a discredit event against her. Forcheville appears only as the object of Swann's wish to separate him from Odette, with no distinct evaluative content of his own.
